text:
Washington is 11-11-0, 3-7-0 in its last ten, and the problem is in net. The Capitals have been an even team on chances, 50.5% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and 54% at five on five, but they have allowed about ten more goals than those chances predict. Charlie Lindgren is .817 and six goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and Logan Thompson was pulled after two goals in 25 seconds against Buffalo. Our playoff odds sit at 42%.

The context everyone knows: Bleacher Nation calls this Alex Ovechkin's final NHL season, and the headlines follow him everywhere, down to his pregame moment with Jayden Daniels at the Commanders game. On the ice he has three points in ten against 4.7 expected, cold by his own standard.

The good news is younger. Ryan Leonard extended his goal streak to four games. Tom Wilson, Pierre-Luc Dubois and Aliaksei Protas have taken 60% of the chances together, and the newer top line of Alex Tuch, Dylan Strome and Jordan Kyrou has created plenty, even if it has been outscored 7-5. Wednesday's 7-3 win over Philadelphia was the version of this team Charlie O'Connor described as running the Flyers out of the building. Spencer Carbery's group is playing well enough to win more often. It needs one of its goalies to give it a few saves back.
headline: Ovechkin's last lap, and a goaltending slide
